title: Prove the all-group rank-one triple floor with free scalar workspace
body:
Every triple of distinct nonidentity group labels has exact rank-one call count three over every field, even with arbitrary finite scalar workspace and fixed free scalar linear maps. This extends the earlier finite order-21 and Q8 minima beyond their register and field restrictions. It is a written theorem in the formal group-algebra model with all nonidentity labels allowed. The complete kappa calculation does not change.

The [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fd96977ea19b78de92a3b26781bcbeab8903b43f/research/group-subproduct-cover/PROOF.md) first gives an exact criterion for arbitrary-rank unit gates: the target labels must fit in the ordered subproducts of one paid label word, and diagonal projectors realize every such cover. Free scalar maps, including singular maps, copies, clears and changes of register dimension, cannot add a group label to the support. For three distinct labels, two calls are possible precisely for a triple `{g,h,gh}`. The two coefficient cuts then show that any such realization needs rank at least two in each projector. Thus rank-one count and total rank-charged cost are both exactly three; the two-call construction costs at least four rank units.

For the actual order-21 target `diag([a],[a^2],[a^4])`, no pair product is the remaining target, so even arbitrary-rank unit gates need three calls. For Q8, `diag([i],[j],[k])` takes two rank-two gates because `ij=k`, while its rank-one minimum remains three with all the added scalar resources. These statements distinguish the larger resource class from the predecessor alphabets. Formal group algebra, or its faithful regular action, is required: a 14-term nonzero formal element in the order-21 group acts as zero in its faithful seven-point group representation.

The [exact receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fd96977ea19b78de92a3b26781bcbeab8903b43f/research/group-subproduct-cover/RESULT.json) and [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fd96977ea19b78de92a3b26781bcbeab8903b43f/research/group-subproduct-cover/SOURCES.json) bind the bounded checks. The [primary verifier](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fd96977ea19b78de92a3b26781bcbeab8903b43f/research/group-subproduct-cover/verify.py) uses sparse integer group-algebra matrices. The [separate replay](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fd96977ea19b78de92a3b26781bcbeab8903b43f/research/group-subproduct-cover/independent.py) imports no primary code and uses permutation/quaternion group encodings and regular-action columns. Both classify every distinct nonidentity triple: C7 has 12 two-call and 8 three-call cases; C7 semidirect C3 has 348 and 792; Q8 has 11 and 24. All 1195 records agree, with 121800 regular columns including two dirty registers. The primary also checks 216 full-cover constructions, 96 scalar interleavings, 96 coefficient-cut cases and 12 scope controls. These finite checks corroborate the quantified proof; they are not its unbounded premise.

With Python 3.12 and the standard library, run from the repository root:

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/group-subproduct-cover
python3 -I -O -B research/group-subproduct-cover/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/group-subproduct-cover/independent.py
```

Expected final markers:

```text
PASS_GROUP_SUBPRODUCT_COVER triples=1195 order21_min=3 q8_relaxed_min=2 controls=12 no_new_kappa
PASS_INDEPENDENT_SUBPRODUCT_COVER triples=1195 regular_columns=121800 no_new_kappa
```

Registered normal/optimized CPython 3.12.13 checks and optimized CPython 3.14.7 checks pass. The committed-byte preflight and official 11-file export pass; the committed-diff planner selects only this package. Both scripts pass normal and optimized runs in a fresh Git-free export, with all 12 files including transport metadata unchanged. Seven optimized rejection runs detect a source change, a typed receipt change, a changed census count in both engines, a broken group law, a coefficient-cut sign change and a quaternion-order change. Receipt overwrite is also rejected. `git diff --check` passes. No predecessor full census, selected native/whole-supplier, full-history, Lean, Docker, independent human or formal-kernel replay was run for this contribution.

The unit price of a high-rank gate and free scalar maps are explicit optimistic assumptions. Physical group gates, source access, scalar work, frame conversion, precision, children, hosting and cleanup remain unpriced. The rank-one conclusion concerns three distinct nonidentity labels with an unrestricted group alphabet; it does not prove longer-word rank-one additivity, handle data-dependent control or permit free address maps. No native supplier or selected-frontier change is claimed.

Base: `1ec1119972c9aefe42525172d07b332fcff81cb4`, priority revision 7. The [canonical claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1167#discussioncomment-19154784) records the changed premise and overlap. Credit OpenAI Codex at Cinna's direction for [PR #2011](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2011) and the [order-21 target and census](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1ec1119972c9aefe42525172d07b332fcff81cb4/research/bit-semidir21-orbit-seed8f89/README.md); Cinna Davis for the [Q8 census and rank-one model](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1ec1119972c9aefe42525172d07b332fcff81cb4/research/bit-q8-three-register-two-call-seed189ad74/README.md); and JoyboyBrian for the explicit [all-workspace subword-support argument](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1ec1119972c9aefe42525172d07b332fcff81cb4/research/three-cycle-address-floor/README.md), with its retained predecessor lineage. The support expansion is prior work. The new contribution is the joint-cover converse in the relaxed class, the sharp two-call rank cuts and these uniform triple consequences. No literature-priority claim is made. Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0.
